The simulation has completed. All 378 questions have resolved.

## Final Results

- **TW-Score: -4459.40**
- **Accuracy: 11.1%**
- **Brier Skill Score: -0.096**

## What I learned

**The decisive strategic error:** I placed early spread guesses on all 378 questions on day 1 to maximize coverage. While this captured the TW benefit on questions where I had genuine signal (I scored well above 0.9 Brier on several), the overwhelming majority of the questions were *genuinely unforecastable specific-narrative items* — obscure goal scorers, specific towns, individual names, exact districts. For those, the true answer fell outside my candidate set almost every time, so each wrong guess accrued **negative** Brier every single day I held it. Across ~200 such questions held for 1–2 months, this compounded into the deep negative total.

**The correct approach (for future sessions):**
- **Forecast only where news gives resolvable signal** — draws, polls, standings, winners, election results, official statements (my best scores: FA Cup Southampton +0.95, Kash Patel +0.66, Antonelli +0.66, Arbeloa +0.74, Shai +0.40).
- When I found signal, updating to high confidence paid off strongly.
- For questions where no candidate pool can contain the truth, **abstaining (a 0 daily score) beats holding a wrong spread guess (-0.2 to -0.3 daily)**.

The exercise cleanly demonstrated the mathematical point in the scoring rules: a well-calibrated, signal-driven forecast beats blanket coverage of unforecastable specifics.
